title: Draft One-Pager: Data Residency + Retention (Hosted / Dedicated / Private)
body:
Redwood Inference — Data Residency + Data Retention (One-Pager, Draft)

Audience: Customer security/compliance reviewers + procurement + technical evaluators
Applies to: Redwood API (Hosted), Redwood Dedicated, Redwood Private (VPC / on-prem)
Last updated (draft): 2026-02-18
Owner: Olga Petrov (GRC). Technical reviewers: Marcus Lin / Kevin Osei. Product alignment: Naomi Feldman.

Important note (use as-is): This document describes current product capabilities and standard operating practices. Some controls vary by deployment mode and contract tier. We do not promise roadmap items in RFP responses; if a requirement appears unsupported, follow the Questionnaire Exceptions Policy / escalate to Security & GRC.

1) Quick summary (customer-friendly)
Redwood supports region-aware deployments and retention controls designed for enterprise workloads.
- Residency: Customers can select the region where inference is processed (Hosted) and where infrastructure is deployed (Dedicated / Private). Options depend on the chosen deployment mode and available regions at time of order.
- Retention: Customer Content retention (prompts/inputs and model outputs) is configurable by deployment mode and contract, with the goal of minimizing retained content while preserving reliability and security logging.
- Logs: Security/audit logs and operational telemetry are retained for a defined period for security, reliability, and billing; retention periods and export options vary by plan.

2) Definitions (use these terms consistently)
Customer Content: The text and files customers submit for inference (inputs/prompts) and the resulting outputs.
Customer Metadata: Account identifiers, request IDs, timestamps, model/version, token counts, error codes, and configuration parameters.
Operational Logs: System/service logs used to operate the platform (e.g., performance metrics, infrastructure events). May include Customer Metadata; should not include full Customer Content except where explicitly configured for debugging.
Audit Logs: Structured records of user/admin actions in Redwood Console/API (e.g., login events, API key changes, RBAC changes, org settings changes, export events).
Processing Region: Region where inference executes and transient data is processed.
Data Residency: Policy/ability to keep processing and/or storage within a specific geography.

3) Region availability (high-level)
Hosted (Redwood API): Customers select a processing region from Redwood-supported cloud regions for the service. Region availability changes over time and is reflected in commercial order forms and/or Console region selectors.
Dedicated: Dedicated clusters are deployed in an agreed cloud region. The region is fixed per cluster unless a new cluster is provisioned.
Private (VPC): Private deployments run in a customer-controlled VPC in an agreed region (cloud) with customer-managed networking boundaries.
Private (on-prem / air-gapped): Available for regulated environments subject to feasibility review.

Approved wording for RFPs (region coverage):
“Redwood supports region selection for inference processing and can deploy Dedicated or Private capacity in specific cloud regions subject to availability and contractual agreement. For strict residency requirements, Redwood Private (VPC or on-prem) provides the strongest residency and isolation controls.”

Do NOT say (anti-claims):
- Do not list specific regions/countries as guaranteed unless the account team confirms current availability.
- Do not claim “global residency” or “any region” support.

4) Data flows by deployment mode (conceptual)
4.1 Hosted (Redwood API)
- Customer sends requests to the Redwood API endpoint for the selected region.
- Inference runs within that region’s serving fleet.
- Customer Content is processed in-memory for inference. Any persistence of Customer Content (if enabled) is controlled by configuration/contract (see Retention section).
- Redwood retains operational metadata for service delivery (e.g., usage/billing, abuse prevention, reliability).

4.2 Dedicated
- Dedicated capacity runs in a reserved environment for a specific customer.
- Inference processing occurs within the cluster’s region.
- Data isolation is improved vs. multi-tenant hosted due to dedicated infrastructure boundaries.
- Logging/telemetry pathways are configurable; Redwood’s control plane may receive health/metrics necessary to operate the service (scope depends on Dedicated architecture and contract).

4.3 Private (VPC)
- Serving plane runs inside the customer’s VPC.
- Network connectivity is customer-managed (e.g., private endpoints/peering) subject to the agreed architecture.
- Control plane interactions (if used) are limited to what is required for provisioning, updates, and health monitoring; the exact data exchanged is deployment-specific and documented in the Private design.

4.4 Private (on-prem)
- Serving components run in the customer environment.
- Data remains within the customer environment except for any explicitly configured support channels (e.g., optional outbound telemetry). Many regulated customers disable outbound telemetry.

TODO (design dependency): Insert diagram from DES-2924 (Hosted vs Private data flow) once available.

5) Data residency controls (what we can commit to)
Hosted
- Processing residency: Requests are processed in the customer-selected region.
- Storage residency: Any persisted service data is managed according to the selected region and Redwood’s service architecture; some limited account-level metadata may be stored/replicated for global service operations depending on configuration. If a customer requires strict “no cross-region storage/replication,” steer to Dedicated or Private.
Dedicated
- Processing + infrastructure residency: Dedicated clusters run in a specified region. Customer-specific infrastructure remains in that region.
- Cross-region dependencies: Any cross-region operations (e.g., backups, control plane operations) must be reviewed per account; do not assume.
Private (VPC / on-prem)
- Strongest residency: Serving plane is within the customer’s network boundary and chosen geography.
- Best fit for: customers with strict regulatory residency requirements, custom retention needs, or highly controlled network policies.

Approved wording (strict residency ask):
“For strict data residency requirements, Redwood Private places the inference serving plane inside your VPC or on-prem environment. Redwood can also deploy Dedicated clusters to a specified region. Hosted processing occurs in the selected region; additional details about metadata/logging and any replication constraints can be reviewed under NDA as part of the security architecture review.”

6) Data retention, deletion, and customer controls
Goal: Minimize retained Customer Content while maintaining secure, reliable operation and meeting contractual obligations.

6.1 Customer Content retention (prompts/outputs)
- Default behavior varies by deployment mode and contract; Redwood does not require long-term retention of Customer Content to provide inference.
- If temporary retention is enabled for debugging/troubleshooting, it is time-bounded and access-controlled.
- Redwood does not use Customer Content to train customer models or general models unless explicitly agreed in writing (see Security FAQ for the precise approved language).

6.2 Customer Metadata + billing records
- Redwood retains usage/billing records and Customer Metadata required for service delivery, fraud/abuse prevention, and accounting.
- Retention duration depends on the record type and contractual/legal requirements.

6.3 Deletion
- Customers may request deletion of retained Customer Content (where applicable) and account data subject to contract and legal obligations.
- Dedicated/Private customers can implement stricter deletion and retention policies depending on architecture (e.g., customer-controlled storage/log sinks).

Approved wording (retention):
“Redwood’s service is designed to minimize retention of Customer Content. Where any content retention is enabled for operational reasons (e.g., troubleshooting), it is time-bounded and access-controlled. Customers can request deletion of retained Customer Content where applicable, subject to contractual and legal requirements. Dedicated and Private deployments provide additional flexibility to meet stricter retention policies.”

7) Audit logs and log export (what customers commonly ask)
Audit logging capabilities (high-level)
- Redwood maintains audit logs for key Console/admin and security-relevant actions (e.g., authentication events, API key lifecycle events, RBAC/SSO settings changes, configuration changes, export events).
- Audit log access is role-controlled (RBAC) and can be exported depending on plan and deployment mode.

Residency angle
- Customers with strict log residency requirements should prefer Dedicated/Private configurations where audit/operational logs can be routed to customer-controlled sinks in-region.

Approved wording (SIEM/log export):
“Redwood supports audit logging for security-relevant actions and provides export options depending on deployment mode and plan. For strict residency requirements, Dedicated and Private can be configured to route logs to customer-controlled destinations within the required region.”

Do NOT say:
- Do not promise a specific SIEM integration by name unless confirmed in the current docs.
- Do not promise “all logs” include “no customer data” without the approved caveat (some logs may include metadata; content logging should be configurable/off by default).

8) Private/VPC option guidance (when to recommend which)
Recommend Hosted when:
- Customer is comfortable with region-selected processing and standard retention/logging controls.
- The primary need is speed-to-value with enterprise-grade controls.

Recommend Dedicated when:
- Customer needs predictable capacity + stronger isolation and more control over region placement.
- Customer has residency requirements that can be met by pinning the environment to a specific cloud region.

Recommend Private (VPC/on-prem) when:
- Customer requires strict residency with customer-managed network boundaries.
- Customer requires custom retention policies, customer-owned log sinks, or limited/no outbound telemetry.
- Customer is in a regulated environment or has procurement mandates for private deployments.

9) RFP response snippets (copy/paste)
Q: “Where is customer data processed and stored?”
A (approved draft): “For Hosted, inference requests are processed in the customer-selected region. Dedicated and Private deployments run in an agreed region (or customer environment for on-prem). Redwood’s service is designed to minimize retention of Customer Content; operational metadata and logs are retained as needed for security, reliability, and billing. Additional architecture details can be reviewed under NDA during the security review.”

Q: “Can you guarantee EU-only residency?”
A (approved draft): “Redwood can support EU-only processing and deployment for certain configurations, subject to region availability and the selected deployment mode. For strict residency requirements, Redwood Private (VPC or on-prem) provides the strongest controls to keep processing and storage within the required geography. Please share your specific requirements (data types, logs, backups, support access) so we can confirm fit.”

Q: “Do you replicate or transfer data cross-region?”
A (approved draft): “Inference processing occurs in the selected/deployed region. Some service metadata and operational signals may be processed to operate and secure the service depending on deployment mode and configuration. If you have strict ‘no cross-region transfer’ requirements, Redwood will review and document the architecture under NDA; Redwood Private can be configured for the strictest controls.”

10) Evidence and review process (how to proceed)
- SOC 2 report and select compliance evidence is available under NDA via the Evidence Request process.
- For strict residency requirements (e.g., regulated financial services), schedule a 30–45 minute architecture/security review with Solutions Engineering + Security.
